title: Split-Beat Driver
constraints: Write `class beat_driver` with `function new(virtual beat_if vif)` and `task drive(bit [31:0] w)`. The constructor drives `valid = 0`.

`drive` sends `w` as **4 byte beats, least significant byte first**, over a valid/ready interface, with `last = 1` on the 4th beat only. A beat transfers on a rising edge with `valid && ready`. Hold `valid`, `data` and `last` stable while `ready = 0`. `drive` returns once the 4th beat has transferred.
When `drive` is called back-to-back and `ready` stays high, beats must go out **every cycle** with no bubbles (at most 2 idle cycles over the whole 100-beat run). No X on the bus.
hints: Drive with nonblocking assignments right after a clock edge, then `do @(posedge vif.clk); while (!vif.ready);` for each beat.
To avoid bubbles between words, don't wait an extra cycle after the last beat. The next `drive` call starts driving immediately, in the same time step.

examples.check: sends 4 beats per word, LSB first
